title: Bulls vs bears
desc: What traders mean by a bull or bear market
intro: I’ll coach you through every lesson. First one: bulls and bears.

cards.title: Bear market, or a bad week?
cards.situation: The market fell 5% this week. A headline shouts “Bear market!” Is it right?

visual.title: Market index fell 5% this week
visual.label: Line chart: the market index falls from 100 at Monday's open to 95 at Friday's close, down 5%

options.feedback: Falling isn’t enough. A bear market is a fall of about 20% from the high. 5% is a normal dip.

options.text: Not yet: it needs a bigger fall
options.feedback: A bad week isn’t a bear market. That takes a fall of about 20% from the high.
A bull market is a rise of about 20% or more. This market fell 5%: a normal dip, not a bull market.

cards.title: Bulls and bears
cards.text: Traders fall into two camps, named after how each animal attacks.

cards.title: Bull market vs bear market
cards.text: A {up}[[bull-market|bull market]]{/up} is a sustained rise of about **20% or more** from a recent low. A {down}[[bear-market|bear market]]{/down} is a sustained fall of about **20% or more** from a recent high.

blocks.tip: A few red days isn’t a bear market. Measure the move in percent.

deeper.title: Why 20%?
deeper.text:
20% is a market convention, not a law. It’s simply the line most traders and news outlets agree on, so everyone means the same thing.

Some analysts use other levels, and a smaller fall of 10% from the high is usually called a **[[correction|correction]]**.
deeper.note: From a high of 100: −10% (90) is a correction. −20% (80) is a bear market.

cards.title: Bull, bear or neither?
cards.q: Drag each move into the right box. Work out the percent first.

items.sub: From a low · over a year

itemFeedback.1,000 → 1,250: 250 on 1,000 is a 25% rise from a low. That’s past the 20% line, so it’s a bull market.
itemFeedback.$50 → $38: $12 off a $50 high is a 24% fall. That’s past the 20% line, so it’s a bear market.

cards.right: Both moves are past the 20% line: one up from a low, one down from a high.

cards.title: Bull market already?
cards.q: A stock rose from **$100** to **$115** this month. Your friend says it’s a bull market. Is he right?

options.feedback: Dollars don’t decide it, the percent does. $15 on a $100 stock is 15%, short of 20%.
The percent decides it. $15 on $100 is 15%, short of the 20% a bull market needs.

options.text: Yes: a month of gains is enough
options.feedback: Time doesn’t decide it, the size of the move does. 15% is short of the 20% line.
A bear market is a fall of about 20% or more. This stock rose 15%.

cards.headline: You can tell a bull market from a bear market.
lines: Bullish means expecting prices to rise. Bearish means expecting them to fall.
A bull or bear market is a move of about 20% or more.
Measure moves in percent, not points or dollars.
